ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, straight lines AB and CD intersect at point O, OE bisects $\angle AOD$, $OF\perp CD$, and $\angle AOE=70^\circ$, find the degree measure of $\angle BOF$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that OE bisects $\angle AOD$ and $\angle AOE = 70^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle AOD = 2\angle AOE = 140^\circ$, \\
since A, O, B are collinear, \\
thus $\angle BOD = \angle AOC = 180^\circ - \angle AOD = 180^\circ - 140^\circ = 40^\circ$, \\
given that $OF \perp CD$, \\
thus $\angle FOD = 90^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle BOF = \angle FOD - \angle BOD = 90^\circ - 40^\circ = \boxed{50^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are two straight lines AB and CD intersecting at point O. AB is basically horizontal, with A on the left and B on the right; CD passes obliquely through O, with C at the lower left and D at the upper right. Ray OE points from O to the upper left, and ray OF points from O to the lower right, and OF is located below OB and is on opposite sides of OB from OD. The problem gives that OE bisects ∠AOD, OF ⟂ CD, and ∠AOE = 70°. Reasoning: Because OE bisects ∠AOD, and ∠AOE = 70°, therefore ∠AOD = 2 × 70° = 140°. Also because A, O, B are on the same straight line, OA and OB are opposite rays, so ∠BOD and ∠AOD are supplementary, ∠BOD = 180° - 140° = 40°. Since OF ⟂ CD, and OD is a ray on the straight line CD, therefore ∠FOD = 90°. Judging from the position in the figure, OB is between OD and OF, therefore ∠BOF = ∠FOD - ∠BOD = 90° - 40° = 50°.
